clue.text: Parallel subject to cover last in seminar

indicators.note: the subject word is to cover, or sit around, the letter taken from seminar

parts.note: a subject under discussion is a topic

indicators.note: last in seminar picks out the final letter of that word

explanation.surface: A school seminar where one parallel subject is covered at the very end of the session.
explanation.definitionFit: Each tropic is a parallel of latitude, Cancer to the north of the equator and Capricorn to the south.

clue.text: Fake, an animistic priest

parts.note: a fake or fraud is a sham

explanation.surface: A bogus holy man of a spirit-worshipping faith is unmasked.
explanation.definitionFit: Animist religions hold that spirits live in nature, and their spiritual healer who deals with those spirits is called by this name.

clue.text: In secret, completely sozzled

definitions.meaning: payments made covertly are said to pass beneath the board where no one sees
someone so drunk they have slid down from their chair to the floor

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both an illicit hidden deal and a drinker who has collapsed beneath the dinner furniture.

clue.text: Old instrument, one telling a story out loud?

indicators.note: out loud says the word for the storyteller is heard rather than written

parts.note: to tell a story can mean to tell a fib, so the teller is a liar

explanation.surface: An ancient bard who recites tales to the strum of an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling a story' looks like a bard narrating, but here it means lying: LIAR, said aloud, gives LYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is a small harp-like stringed instrument from ancient Greece.

clue.text: Blooming thing, an avalanche?

definitions.meaning: a flower, here the small white bloom of late winter
a whimsical reading: an avalanche is a fall of snow from a mountainside

explanation.definitionFit: The white winter flower's name, split in two, describes a mass of snow tumbling downhill.

clue.text: Wearer of bladed footwear — a slipper?

definitions.meaning: someone in ice boots with metal runners
a whimsical reading: one who slips and glides across ice

explanation.definitionFit: Someone gliding on ice wears blades on their boots and is, playfully, a person who slides about.

clue.text: Plan to take some fag-end away

indicators.note: take some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A resolution to give up smoking by throwing the last cigarette butt away.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'fag-end' is British slang for a cigarette butt.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a programme or list of things one intends to do, so a schedule or scheme.

clue.text: Vessel carrying right banner

indicators.note: the ship is carrying the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a vessel here is a ship, such as a steam-powered one

explanation.surface: A ship sails with the correct flag flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow flag or pennant fluttering from a mast is called a streamer, a kind of banner.

clue.text: Choose a tool

definitions.meaning: to choose is to select
a pointed digging implement, as used by miners

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning select and the name of a pointed implement for breaking ground.

clue.text: One who informs the referee?

definitions.meaning: someone who exposes wrongdoing within an organisation
a whimsical reading: an official who blows a whistle to stop play

explanation.definitionFit: An insider who exposes misconduct is so called, and a football official literally blows the little pipe.

clue.text: Part of a stag is learnt about

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of learnt are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has studied some feature of a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag's branched horn is called an antler, one of the pair it grows each year.

clue.text: Odd parts of bird bearing the white meat?

indicators.note: the odd parts are the first and third letters of the word bird

parts.note: a compass bearing such as east

explanation.surface: Choosing the bits of a roast fowl that carry the pale meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' and 'bearing' look like they belong to one phrase, but 'Odd parts of' works only on bird; EAST comes separately from 'bearing'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a chicken or turkey the chest portion is the pale flesh, as opposed to the dark leg meat.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink with no head is hot

indicators.note: with no head says the drink's first letter is removed

parts.note: brandy is a distilled alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A spirit served without a frothy top turns out to be warming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests the foam on a beer, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy and hot are both slang for sexually aroused or lustful.

clue.text: This time, something gifted

definitions.meaning: the time now, as opposed to past or future
a gift given to someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the current moment and a gift handed over.

clue.text: Minor injury reduced

definitions.meaning: a small wound such as a nick to the skin
lowered, as prices are when slashed

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small gash in the skin and something lowered, like a price.

clue.text: Goats sure to destroy old lizard

indicators.note: to destroy something is to wreck it, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Livestock certain to be wiped out by an ancient reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: A plated dinosaur from the Jurassic; dinosaur itself means terrible lizard, so this is an ancient one.

clue.text: A district gets the prize

parts.note: a ward is an electoral district of a town

explanation.surface: One local area wins the trophy in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition of merit.

clue.text: In summation, nothing more to say?

definitions.meaning: in total, when everything is counted up
a whimsical reading: every part of the tale has now been recounted

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means altogether, and read literally says the whole story has been related.

clue.text: Motorbike, a confusing machine?

definitions.meaning: a lightweight motorcycle built for rough off-road tracks
a whimsical reading: a device that jumbles things, such as one that encrypts signals

explanation.definitionFit: It names both an off-road motorcycle and any device that mixes up or encodes signals.

clue.text: Thicken stews — here?

indicators.note: stews means stirs about, so the letters of the first word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook wonders where a thickened stew is made.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: thickening stews is done in the room it names.
explanation.definitionFit: Stews are thickened in the room of a house where food is prepared and cooked.

clue.text: Old tramp heading for Edinburgh set off

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or old
to tramp is to walk heavily, to plod

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A former hike towards the Scottish capital sets out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' looks like a vagrant noun, but it is the verb, a heavy walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to detonate it, making it blow up.

clue.text: Comfort blanket's second, as support for artist

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of the word blanket

explanation.surface: A security blanket acts as a backup prop for a nervous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comfort blanket' reads as one phrase, but it splits: EASE, then the second letter of 'blanket'.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter rests the canvas on this wooden stand while working.

clue.text: Musical game

definitions.meaning: a stage show by Benny and Björn of ABBA with Tim Rice
a board game of kings, queens and pawns

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a board game of strategy and a 1980s stage musical about a championship.

clue.text: Float up and down, up and down!

definitions.meaning: to float on water, like a cork on a fishing line

definitions.text: up and down, up and down!
definitions.meaning: a quick repeated bouncing motion, as a head nods; the letters also read the same up or down the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition doubles as a joke: in a Down entry these letters read the same from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cork bobs: it floats while moving gently and repeatedly upward and back on the water.
